title: Relaxed and rotational Gaussian surface areas
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $A\subseteq\bbr^n$ be measurable. The relaxed Gaussian surface area of $A$, defined by taking the infimum over smooth sequences of functions valued in $[0,1]$ that converge to the indicator of $A$ in Gaussian $L^1$ and whose coordinate derivatives are Gaussian-square-integrable, of the corresponding limit inferior of their integrated Gaussian gradient lengths, equals the Gaussian surface area defined by the limit inferior of the normalized disagreement probability under infinitesimal Gaussian rotations.
